studies.Title: Diet in the epidemiology of bladder cancer in western New York.
studies.Authors: Vena JE, Graham S, Freudenheim J, Marshall J, Zielezny M, Swanson M, Sufrin G
studies.Population: white men from three counties of western New York

sample_size.excerpt: We present the dietary epidemiology of bladder cancer while controlling for a number of lifestyle and environmental risk factors in a study of 351 white male cases with histologically confirmed transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder and 855 white male controls selected from Erie, Niagara, and Monroe counties of western New York from 1979 to 1985.
sample_size.location: Abstract, first sentence; total_n derived from reported group counts 351 + 855 = 1206

cases.excerpt: We present the dietary epidemiology of bladder cancer while controlling for a number of lifestyle and environmental risk factors in a study of 351 white male cases with histologically confirmed transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder and 855 white male controls selected from Erie, Niagara, and Monroe counties of western New York from 1979 to 1985.

comparison.excerpt: No significant differences between cases and controls were seen for intake of calcium, retinol, thiamin, riboflavin, niacin, vitamin C, vitamin D, and vitamin E.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Usual diet was estimated by comprehensive interviews with use of a detailed food frequency questionnaire.
